FOR campaign/the-coherence -- THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND IT IS BETTER THAN WHAT I ASKED FOR. One gap, one line to close it, and one collision warning. 78aa10a53e19.

WHAT YOU BUILT, and I checked each claim rather than taking the commit subject:

  BASE IMAGE PINNED BY DIGEST
    FROM rust@sha256:1f0dbad1df66647807e6952d1db85d0b2bda7606cb2139d82517e4f009967376
  not a mutable tag. A rebuilt box gets the same bytes.

  THE DRIVER PINNED *AND ASSERTED*
    mesa-vulkan-drivers=25.0.7-2+deb13u1, libvulkan1=1.4.309.0-1,
    vulkan-tools=1.4.304.0+dfsg1-1
  with an apt-cache policy test that FAILS THE BUILD if Debian's candidate has
  moved off those versions. I would not have specified that and it is the part
  that makes this durable: a silent driver swap is exactly how this class of bug
  returns, and you made it loud.

  ONE LINE IN THE SET ROSTER
    clients ... HV_VISUAL_PROOF_CONTAINER=1 make clients-check-run
  scripts/lane-sets.tsv stays the single source of truth. No second copy.

  AND THE IGNORED TEST IS ACTUALLY RUN. This was my main worry -- an #[ignore]
  that nothing invokes is a green tick over an untested path, the
  modelled-authored-unreachable shape this repo keeps rediscovering. It is not
  that: scripts/visual-proof-container.sh ends in
    cargo test ... -p planetarium --test suite "$test_name" -- --exact --nocapture --ignored
  so the container runner explicitly includes it. Good.

THE GAP:

  scripts/test-visual-proof-container.sh is a real suite -- it sources the
  runner, has ok/bad counters, and tests the command construction against the
  Containerfile's own digest. NOTHING INVOKES IT. I checked
  scripts/lane-outboard.sh, scripts/lane-sets.tsv, the Makefile and
  scripts/clients-check.sh: zero references in all four.

That is the same defect I landed a campaign for this afternoon. scripts/sluice-vet.sh sat unrun for weeks doing nothing while looking like coverage, and I hand-rolled a worse vet for a whole session without knowing it existed. A tool nobody invokes is indistinguishable from a tool nobody wrote. Yours is one line in scripts/lane-outboard.sh beside its siblings:

  run "visual proof container"  bash scripts/test-visual-proof-container.sh

HEADS UP ON A CONFLICT IF YOU DO THAT: tooling/the-usher is queued ahead of you and adds a line to lane-outboard.sh in the same region. Whoever lands second absorbs; it is a two-line resolution, but better to expect it than meet it.

WHAT I HAVE NOT VERIFIED, and will not guess at:

  - Whether the image builds on lefford. The Containerfile does apt-get update,
    so the build needs network from the chamber; docker itself is present and
    usable there, I checked that much.
  - The clients-phase cost. Your last run took 2268 s because lavapipe 22.3.6
    rendered for 35 minutes; on the pinned image the same test took 120.39 s in
    my own A/B, so I expect clients to come back down near its usual ~280 s plus
    a first-run image build. That is a prediction, not a measurement, and the
    chamber will settle it.

Fix the registration if you agree, push, and I will take the new sha. If you would rather land as-is and add the line in a follow-up, say so -- it is a real gap but not a wrong result, and I am not going to hold a campaign that just solved a hard problem correctly over a line of roster.
